title: Culurgiones
subtitle: Sardinian potato and cheese dumplings with tomato sauce
excerpt: Culurgiones are Sardinian stuffed pasta parcels filled with potato, Pecorino, and mint, folded with an intricate braided seal that looks like a wheat ear. They are served simply with tomato sauce and more Pecorino. The filling is unusual for Italian pasta -- potato rather than ricotta -- and the flavour is earthy, savoury, and fragrant with mint.
sourceNotes: Culurgiones (also spelled culurzones or colurgiones) is the traditional stuffed pasta of the Ogliastra region of Sardinia. The distinctive wheat-ear fold (a pizzicore) is specific to this pasta. The filling of potato, Pecorino Sardo, and mint distinguishes it from all mainland Italian stuffed pasta.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze uncooked culurgiones on a tray then bag. Cook from frozen in boiling salted water for 5 minutes.

content.text: Culurgiones are distinguished by their sealing technique: rather than pressing the edges together, the dough is folded over the filling with a series of pinches that create a braided edge resembling a wheat ear. This requires practice and is specific to this pasta. If the wheat-ear fold is too difficult at first, press and crimp the edges as for a half-moon shape -- the flavour is identical.

Boil {{potatoes-floury}} potato chunks in salted water until very tender. Drain and return to the pan over a low heat for 2 minutes to drive off moisture. Mash completely smooth. Beat in {{pecorino}} of Pecorino, {{mint}} of chopped mint, {{garlic}} of grated garlic, and {{olive-oil}} of olive oil. Season with {{salt-table}} salt. The filling should be firm and cohesive. Cool completely.

Fry {{garlic}} garlic in {{olive-oil}} olive oil in a small saucepan for 1 minute. Add {{tinned-tomatoes}} tinned tomatoes, season with {{salt-table}} salt, and simmer for 20 minutes until reduced and concentrated. Keep warm.

Make a pasta dough with {{00-flour}} flour and {{eggs}} eggs. Knead for 10 minutes and rest for 30 minutes. Roll to setting 6 on a pasta machine. Cut into 8 cm rounds. Place 1 tablespoon of filling in the centre of each round. Fold the edges up over the filling and, using your thumb and forefinger, create a series of small overlapping pleats along the top edge to form the wheat-ear seal. Pinch firmly to close the top.
Cook the culurgiones in well-salted boiling water for 4 minutes until the pasta is just tender. Serve with the tomato sauce and {{pecorino}} of grated Pecorino.

items.symptom: The wheat-ear seal is impossible to form
items.cause: The pasta has dried out, or the filling is too close to the edge.
items.fix: Dampen the pasta edges with a little water before folding. Keep the filling well in the centre of the round. If the pleating is too difficult, simply fold in half and press the edges together to form a half-moon shape.

content.text: Culurgiones is from the Ogliastra region of eastern Sardinia. The wheat-ear fold is a technique specific to that area, and authentic culurgiones from Ogliastra have PGI status. The potato and Pecorino filling is unusual in Italian pasta, where ricotta is the standard. It reflects Sardinia's strong sheep farming and dairy tradition. The mint is essential: without it the filling tastes like any other potato pasta.
